mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the chromosome sets was most worthwhile: the planned sequence distinguishes sister-copy separation and nuclear-envelope formation from the later splitting of cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial membrane and cytoplasm fittings were repetitive and gave little immediate detail about how growth occurs.

surprise.text: The replication inset clarified that DNA amount doubles while the sister chromosome copies remain joined before separation.

arbitrary.text: The fittings had clear purposes, though adding proteins as a single cytoplasm-growth slot simplified the process without explaining much about it.

continue.text: I would cautiously continue: the separation sequence was clear and the descendants suggest further branches, though I would hope for more explanation than the initial fittings provided.
